AD Methodology.description: Structured Active Directory penetration testing methodology — from external recon to domain compromise.

steps.task: Identify domain name and domain controllers (nmap, nslookup, dig)
Enumerate DNS records (A, MX, SRV, TXT) — dig axfr, dnsx
Identify netblock ranges (ARIN, Shodan, Censys)
Search for exposed credentials (DeHashed, HaveIBeenPwned, GitHub)
OSINT user enumeration — LinkedIn, hunter.io, theHarvester
NetBIOS & SMB enumeration — nbtscan, enum4linux-ng
LDAP anonymous bind — ldapsearch -x -h {DC} -b 'dc=,dc='
Identify null session access — nxc smb {target} -u '' -p ''
Enumerate domain password policy before spraying
Identify pre-auth disabled accounts for AS-REP roasting
Password spraying with Kerbrute or NetExec (respect lockout threshold)
AS-REP roasting — GetNPUsers.py (no creds needed)
LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning with Responder if on same network segment
SMB relay attack if SMB signing disabled — nxc smb {range} --gen-relay-list
Exploit exposed services (CVE hunting on identified versions)
BloodHound collection — bloodhound-python -c All
Kerberoasting — GetUserSPNs.py / Rubeus kerberoast
Analyze BloodHound — find shortest path to Domain Admin
Check ACL misconfigurations (GenericAll, WriteDacl, GenericWrite)
Enumerate unconstrained / constrained / RBCD delegation
Hunt for credentials in shares, scripts, SYSVOL, NETLOGON
Check GPO permissions — can you write a GPO applied to DAs?
Exploit ACL path found in BloodHound
Abuse delegation (unconstrained, constrained, RBCD)
Exploit writable GPO linked to OU containing DAs
Pass-the-Hash or Pass-the-Ticket with stolen credentials
Shadow Credential attack via Whisker
Abuse AdminSDHolder if WriteDacl on it
RBCD attack — create/modify machine account (MachineAccountQuota > 0): addcomputer.py; set msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity; S4U2Self+S4U2Proxy to impersonate DA on target
DCSync — dump all hashes (secretsdump.py / lsadump::dcsync)
Dump KRBTGT hash for Golden Ticket creation
Compromise forest trust (SID History, inter-forest trust abuse)
Document all findings and attack paths
Enumerate AD CS — Certify.exe find /vulnerable or certipy find -u user -p pass -dc-ip {DC}
ESC1 — enroll certificate with SAN set to DA UPN — certipy req -ca {CA} -template {template} -upn administrator@{domain}
ESC4 — modify vulnerable template permissions to gain write access then exploit as ESC1
ESC6 — CA has EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 — enroll any cert with SAN
ESC8 — NTLM relay to AD CS HTTP endpoint (/certsrv/certfnsh.asp) — coerce auth then relay
Authenticate with obtained certificate via PKINIT — certipy auth -pfx cert.pfx -dc-ip {DC}
Golden Certificate — forge cert with stolen CA key (certipy forge)
ESC2 — template allows Any Purpose EKU or no EKU; enroll and use for authentication: certipy req -ca {CA} -template {ESC2_template}

ESC3 — enrollment agent template abuse; request cert on behalf of DA using two-step enrollment: certipy req -ca {CA} -template {EnrollmentAgent}; certipy req -ca {CA} -template User -on-behalf-of {DA}
Certifried (CVE-2022-26923) — create machine account, set dNSHostName to DA hostname, request computer certificate that maps to DA: certipy account create + certipy req
Golden Ticket — forge with KRBTGT hash (10-year lifetime)
Diamond Ticket (harder to detect than Golden)
AdminSDHolder backdoor (propagates to all protected objects)
DSRM password set for offline DC admin access
SID History injection on a regular user account
Shadow Credentials via msDS-KeyCredentialLink write — Whisker.exe add /target:DA
